overclaims: Marcus does not define a 'proper model', and no public test separates systems that have one from systems that lack one.
Whether LLMs build internal world models is itself disputed, so no system can be agreed to be on either side of the line.
checks.note: The packet establishes no agreed operational test, not the absence of every public test or the impossibility of agreement about any system. The dispute assertion appears in the contract but lacks supporting evidence. Scope these statements to the supplied evidence and undefined criteria.

The normalized proposition drops the claim that unreliability is increasingly evident. The payload correctly discloses that this trend was not assessed, but the proposition should preserve it while keeping the assessment explicitly limited to the existence of problems.

overclaims: Benchmarks on temporal reasoning exist, but none tie their results to chess-rule competence in the same system.
checks.note: Only one temporal benchmark was considered. Its lack of paired chess testing supports saying no matching evaluation was found in this search, not that none exists. The assessment, conditional structure, and open horizon otherwise match the frozen case.

The payload preserves the comparison, explains the missing common metric, and correctly distinguishes the studies found from matched evaluations of human speech and action. The assessment matches the reviews.
